# `exposed-private-error-set`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: strict · Default: off · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports a public function signature that names a private error-set declaration.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

The error set is part of the function's contract, but a private declaration
keeps it out of the documented API. Error values are global, so callers can
still match each error by name; what they cannot do is refer to the set itself,
to reuse it in their own signatures or find it in the generated documentation.
This is API-design guidance enabled by the `strict` profile, not a correctness
diagnostic.

## When it fires

Named local error sets are checked; anonymous structural error sets and
unresolved inferred sets are left alone.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const Error = error{Boom};

pub fn run() Error!void {
    return error.Boom;
}
```
